memory_boundary: Memory-only source-discovery leads; no external search, Evidence search, current employer/nationality/wage lookup or labor-law verification.

leads.memory: Ship ownership, technical management and crew management can be organizationally separated; a crew manager may handle recruitment, contracts, payroll, travel, training records and relief planning across fleets without owning the vessel.
Manning or recruitment agencies connect ship managers with regional seafarer labor pools and can become important gatekeepers for screening, documentation, placement and replacement capacity.

Crew supply is constrained by rank, certificate, vessel-type experience and sea-time rather than raw headcount; senior officers or specialized endorsements can be scarce even when entry-level labor is abundant.

Maritime academies/training centers, simulators, examinations, onboard cadet berths and accumulated sea service form a multi-stage pipeline; bottlenecks today can surface as officer shortages years later.
Medical fitness, passports, visas, seafarer documents and flag/port acceptance can gate deployment even after a person is hired and technically competent.

Crew rotation depends on synchronized relief availability, flights, port access, immigration, agents and vessel schedule; a failed relief plan can extend tours and reduce resilience without any change in nominal fleet size.

Base wages, overtime/leave structures, allotments, collective bargaining and agency/management arrangements create a distinct labor-cost and contract layer; exact scales and legal effect require later Evidence.

Manning level, watch schedules, port workload and extended tours interact with fatigue and work/rest compliance; labor shortage can therefore propagate into operational and casualty risk rather than only higher wage expense.

Attrition of experienced officers raises more than replacement cost: promotion pipelines, vessel-specific knowledge and mentoring capacity can erode, making retention a slow-moving operational constraint.

Accommodation, food, communications access, shore leave, onboard social conditions and support services influence retention and tour acceptability; these are operational labor-market inputs rather than purely social side notes.
Financial distress can surface through delayed wages, repatriation problems or crews left without normal support, linking owner/counterparty solvency to labor continuity and regulatory intervention.

Seafaring labor supply has strong regional and historical specialization; language, training institutions, agency networks and promotion paths create path dependence, but country-by-country rankings are too brittle for blind recall.

Crew change is a cross-layer transaction involving operator/crew manager, local agent, transport, hotel/medical providers and border/port authorities; administrative readiness can be as binding as physical access.
The atlas effective-versus-nominal-capacity concept extends to labor: a seaworthy vessel without the required qualified crew or timely relief is not fully deployable capacity.
Operating-cost analysis should separate wages/benefits, travel/relief, training, recruitment and management fees because labor shocks can move these components differently.

The atlas counterparty-risk lead includes crew consequences: insolvency or weak cash management can interrupt wages, travel, victualing or repatriation before a vessel itself becomes physically unavailable.
Port and border restrictions can create a labor-side bottleneck by preventing routine relief, even when cargo handling and berth operations remain available.
Rules can change effective supply through operating constraints; this general mechanism already exists in the atlas and is not a separate labor category.
Crew records and notices have known-time issues, but the general point-in-time information principle is already represented in the atlas.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Current shares and rankings are dynamic and require source-first Evidence.
Exact rates, clauses and applicability are precision-fragile.
Detailed rule versions and flag acceptance require authoritative documents.
Company performance and causal attribution require claim-scoped Evidence.

method_observation.observation: Labor recall is most useful when modeled as a pipeline from recruitment through qualification, deployment, relief and retention; it degrades into stereotypes or fragile rankings when organized by nationality or employer.

deferred_precision: company-specific labor practice and incident findings
